contents_drawer:
The drawer runs in `Showcase.ts` without the engine. Every listener carries the mount's `AbortController` signal, so `destroy` removes them.

**Open.** The `Contents` link's click handler calls `preventDefault` and toggles the drawer. `#fold(open)` does three things:
- toggles `show` on `#contents-panel`;
- sets `aria-expanded`;
- swaps `text-body-emphasis` for `active` on the link, the pressed look the choices use.

Bootstrap's `.offcanvas-lg` rules do the rest (built sheet `dist/src/bootstrap/index.css`:6377-6436):
- Under lg the panel is `position: fixed`, `visibility: hidden`, `translateX(-100%)`.
- With `show` it is visible and slides in over `transform 0.3s ease-in-out`, with `transition: none` under reduced motion.
- It is full width at 390 (`max-width: 100%`) and 400 px wide from 576 to 991.
- From lg no `.offcanvas-lg` visibility or transform rule applies. The panel is the in-flow sticky sidebar with a transparent background, and the link does not render.

**Fold.** Every route folds at once, with no slide-out. A landing therefore shows immediately, the next Tab stop is visible, and no `transitionend` bookkeeping exists. The five routes:
1. A click on a hash link in the panel. The default navigation proceeds, so Chromium's fragment anchor clears focus and sets the sequential focus starting point on the section. The arrangers' Tab-after-click depends on this.
2. Escape on the document while open. Focus moves to the `Contents` link.
3. `focusout` from the panel when `relatedTarget` is an element outside both the panel and the link. A null `relatedTarget`, such as from a click on a group label, keeps it open.
4. A document click outside both the panel and the link. A face or theme button click therefore folds it.
5. `#offset` reading the panel's position as no longer `fixed`, which happens when the viewport reaches lg. This is the same check the engine's Offcanvas resize handler makes (src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:71-80).

**Focus.**
- Opening leaves focus on the link (the disclosure pattern). The panel follows the header in DOM order, so the next Tab reaches `Containers`, and Shift+Tab from `Containers` returns to the link with the drawer still open.
- There is no focus trap, `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal` or backdrop. J8's arrival readings therefore stay `countDialogs() === 0` and `collectOverlays()` empty.
- The engine never binds the panel. The offcanvas plugin acts only on `[data-bs-toggle="offcanvas"]` and boots `.offcanvas.show` (src/browser/plugins.ts:246-269), and the panel has neither the `.offcanvas` class nor any `data-bs-*` attribute.
- The responsive hide matches only `[aria-modal]` elements (Offcanvas.ts:76).

**Active section.**
- One IntersectionObserver with rootMargin `0px 0px -75% 0px` (the top quarter, the band J3's landing reads) observes the 72 `main > div > section` elements.
- The link to the last intersecting section, in page order, gets `aria-current="location"` and `fw-semibold`, and `link-underline-opacity-100` replaces `link-underline-opacity-0`. The previous link loses all three. When no section intersects, the mark stays where it was.
- When the marked link is outside the panel's scrollport, Showcase sets the panel's `scrollTop` to bring it into view. This covers the lg sidebar and the drawer on open. It never calls `scrollIntoView`, which would also scroll the document and move the J3 landing.
- `destroy` disconnects the observer.

**Back to contents:** none. The sticky `Contents` link under lg and the sticky sidebar from lg reach the index in one step from any scroll position. Per-section back links would add 72 tab stops and 72 controls to main, the refusal walk and the pointer census.

**How each step that reaches a Contents link changes:**
- **J1:** under lg it reads the region with no rendered nav and the link `collapsed`, clicks `Contents`, reads `expanded`, then runs the existing text and one-nav readings. It places `contents-index` and the added `contents-drawer`.
- **J2:** at 390 the expected focus sequence becomes skip link, Bootstrap, Tailwind, no layer, Tailwind + layer, Light, Dark, link `Contents`. It presses Enter, reads `expanded`, and Tab reaches link `Containers`. Escape then returns focus to `Contents` reading `collapsed` before the `Email address` traversal. The Shift+Tab counts of 4 and 5 stay.
- **J3:** under lg it calls `openContents()` before each of the 72 links and reads the drawer `collapsed` after each click.
- **Variant case:** it calls `openContents()` before `collectContrastSubjects()`.
- **Arrangers:** the seven `clickAccessibleWithin('Contents', 'link', …)` calls become `clickContents(…)`, at setupBrowser.ts:3832, :4110, :4489, :4509, :4719, :5203 and :5796.

contents_drawer:
The drawer is a native `details` element. It needs no script, no engine, no `collapse` class and no dialog. Markup, built in `createShell` with `buildElement`:

```html
<details class="d-lg-none">
  <summary class="py-2 mb-3 fw-semibold border-bottom">Contents</summary>
  <nav>(unchanged createContents output)</nav>
</details>
```

Behavior:
- **Folded on arrival:** below `lg`, the drawer shows one row. The browser draws a disclosure marker on the summary (`display: list-item`, set by Bootstrap reboot and by Tailwind preflight under all three faces) and flips it when the drawer opens.
- **Opening:**
  - a click opens it, and Enter or Space on the focused summary does too;
  - the index opens in place, under the summary, in two columns (three from `md`);
  - it stays open after a section is picked.
- **Hidden content:** while folded, the 72 links are not rendered. `checkVisibility()` reads false, so `isRendered` and `isReachable` read false and the links are neither tab stops nor pointer targets.
- **From `lg`:** the `d-lg-none` class hides the whole drawer, and the sticky sidebar takes over.

Why each constraint holds:
- **No engine.** The chrome needs no engine: the `details` element is native, so J2, J6 and J7 mount without one.
- **No dialog.** No `role="dialog"` element exists at rest, so J8 still reads `countDialogs()` as 0.
- **No `collapse` class.** No `.collapse` class is involved, so the drawer survives the `Tailwind, no layer` face, where `collapse` reads `visibility: collapse`.
- **No reserved name.** The names `Sections` and `Open the … drawer` are not reused.
- **Shared names.** The summary's shared names are `py-2` and `mb-3`. The header and fragments already use both, so the partition's per-name rows hold, but the summary adds one signature key.
- **Component names.** The drawer carries no component name, so the preservation `excluded` count holds.

Test helpers, added to /home/user/veneer/tests/setupBrowser.ts beside `collectContrastSubjects` (:1368), each with TSDoc:
- `openContents()` resolves the Contents region and its `details` child, and refuses when either is missing.
  - It does nothing when the `details` element is not rendered (from `lg`) or is already open.
  - Otherwise it calls `clickDisclosure('Contents')` and waits under `COMPONENT_WAIT` until `open` is true.
- `clickContentsLink(name)` awaits `openContents()`, then calls `clickAccessibleWithin('Contents', 'link', name)`.

These replace the bare Contents clicks. A person at 390 must open the drawer before choosing a section, and the helper does exactly that. At 1280 it adds nothing.

Capture states:
- **`contents-arrival` (added):** the Contents region on arrival. At 390 it shows the folded drawer; at 1280, the sidebar region.
- **`contents-index` (existing):** keeps its subject, the one rendered `nav`. J1 places it after the open step at 390, so at 390 it captures the open drawer's index.

Together the two states give the design review both the folded and the open drawer.
isolation:
Sections are isolated by a rule without any horizontal inset. Every section except the last in its group gets `pb-4` and `border-bottom` beside its existing `mb-5`:
- each section reads as a frame: content, then 1.5rem, then a full-width rule, then 3rem before the next title;
- the group's last section needs no rule, because the next group's `h2` (`mt-5 pt-4 mb-4 pb-2 border-bottom`) supplies the boundary;
- 63 of the 72 sections carry the rule (72 sections less 9 groups).

Two constraints fix the shape:
- **Rule at the bottom, not the top.** The hash target of a Contents link is the `section`, and `scroll-padding-top` (header height plus 8 px) lands its top. open_rulings:
What 'each thing isolated' means. Options:
- (a) Rule-delimited sections in one document. Recommended: it moves only the partition signature rows.
- (b) One section per view. This breaks J3, the census, containment, partition, preservation and every component table.
- (c) A padded card frame per section. This narrows the content box and moves the scrollspy-1280 and scrollspy-390 rows, the no-matrix-scroll-at-1280 claim and the containment geometry.

Where the mobile drawer sits. Options:
- In the page flow, folded on arrival. Recommended: no contract moves.
- A bar that stays under the header. This needs observer-written `top` and `max-height` on a second element, which changes the inline-style-at-rest contract (integration.test.ts:1210-1222, veneer.md:2624-2626). The scroll offset must add the bar's height, which moves the 8 px landing at 390 (Showcase.test.ts:701-775, setupBrowser.test.ts:3380-3435). It also risks covering pointer targets.

Whether the drawer folds after a section is picked. Options:
- Stays open. Recommended: no script, and J3 opens it once.
- Folds on pick. This needs a click listener in `Showcase.ts`; J3 then opens the drawer before each of its 72 picks, and the guide gains a behavior claim with its case.

Whether stage B surfaces may appear in the showcase at all, and whether a native-surface fence may load there (verdict:1156; remainder-map-2026-10-04.md:97). The reserved Interactions-group slot assumes factory-created leaves and no fence.

How the user views each round on a phone. The repository is private and Pages is off. Recommended: a private Artifact holding the committed bytes, republished in place each round, plus `git pull` and opening the file on desktop.
